identity.title: Are High-redshift Galaxies Hot? Temperature of z > 5 Galaxies and Implications for Their Dust Properties

paper_type_evidence.quote: The three analogs of high-redshift galaxies have been observed with ALMA in Band 3 (ID: 2012.1.00919.S, PI: Y. Kakazu)

evidence.quote: The sample consists of 9 star-forming Lyman Break galaxies at $1-4$ $L^*_{\rm UV}$ (the characteristic knee of the galaxy luminosity function) and one low luminosity quasar (*HZ5*) at redshifts $5.1 < z < 5.7$.

question.value: Do normal z>5 galaxies have warmer IR SEDs than assumed, and can this plus altered dust geometry explain their low IRX at given beta?

evidence.quote: The trends in this sample suggest that normal high-redshift galaxies have a warmer infrared (IR) SED compared to average $z<4$ galaxies that are used as prior in these studies.
observed with ALMA in Band 3 (ID: 2012.1.00919.S, PI: Y. Kakazu)

bands.value: Band 3 (analogs); Band 7 [CII] at rest 158 um for z~5.5 sample

evidence.quote: observed with ALMA in Band 3 (ID: 2012.1.00919.S, PI: Y. Kakazu) centered at an observed frequency of $92\,{\rm GHz}$
corresponds to the rest-frame wavelength of CO$(1-0)$ emission ($2.6\,{\rm mm}$)

continuum_bandwidth.value: 2.0 GHz in each of three line-free spectral windows (TDM); line FDM 0.9375 GHz

evidence.quote: the continuum observations use the “time division mode” with a bandwidth of $2.0\,{\rm GHz}$ in each of the three line-free spectral windows
The synthesized beam sizes are on average $3.5\ensuremath{''} \times 2.5\ensuremath{''}$.
All three galaxies are undetected in the continuum around rest-frame $2.6\,{\rm mm}$ at $\lesssim50\,{\rm \mu Jy}$ at $3\sigma$
The integration times vary between $1255\,{\rm s}$ and $9852\,{\rm s}$ and the number of antennae between 24 and 36

evidence.quote: Figure [2] shows the optical images by *HST*’s *Advanced Camera for Survey* (ACS) in F814W ($I$-band) at $200\,{\rm pc}$ resolution.

**Temperature constraints on high-z galaxies from (cite: PAVESI16)**

analysis_steps.goal: Fit IR SEDs of analogs and local galaxies

method.value: Casey (2012) graybody + mid-IR power-law fit to 24-500 um photometry; lambda0 fixed at 200 um

evidence.quote: we fix the wavelength at which the optical depth is unity to $\lambda_{0}=200\,{\rm \mu m}$

key_parameters.value: beta_IR free; also fixed 1.6 and 2.0 as test

evidence.quote: we also fit the photometry with a fixed $\beta_{\rm IR}$ of $1.6$ and $2.0$

validation.value: no significant differences with fixed beta_IR

evidence.quote: we do not find any significant differences in the following results and conclusions

method.value: BC03 templates with emission lines, Levenberg-Marquardt, Monte Carlo errors

evidence.quote: The fit is performed using a Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, as part of the `R/minpack.lm` package

evidence.loc: Physical properties from optical SED fitting
evidence.quote: The fit is performed using a Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, as part of the `R/minpack.lm` package

validation.value: photometric vs spectroscopic Halpha EW agree within 25%

evidence.quote: we find an agreement on the order of $25\%$ or better between the photometrically and spectroscopically measured H$\alpha$ EW and line ratios

analysis_steps.goal: Recompute L_FIR of z~5.5 galaxies with warm prior

method.value: Casey SED normalized to 158 um continuum, T=60-90 K, marginalized over alpha and beta_IR, integrated 3-1100 um

evidence.quote: The total FIR luminosity is derived by integration between $3\,{\rm \mu m}$ and $1100\,{\rm \mu m}$
The result is marginalized over a grid of mid-IR slopes and emissivities ($1.5 < \alpha < 2.5$, $1.0 < \beta_{\rm IR} < 2.0$).

assumptions.value: temperature prior 60-90 K extrapolated from local trends and analogs

evidence.quote: the applied warm IR SED prior is motivated by the extrapolation of trends found in local galaxy samples as well as three low-redshift analogs
The data are reduced using the standard `CASA` ALMA calibration pipeline.

used_for.value: subtract neighbor flux before aperture photometry

evidence.quote: use `GALFIT` (cite: CHIEN11) to carefully subtract the flux of the neighboring galaxies
as part of the `R/minpack.lm` package
We find temperatures ranging from $70\,{\rm K}$ to $100\,{\rm K}$ with uncertainties of $\sim 10\,{\rm K}$
which, as expected, are increased by $\sim0.6\,{\rm dex}$

findings_qualitative.value: Even with maximally warm SED, some z>5 galaxies remain below minimum IRX-beta relation of standard dust models

evidence.quote: Despite this, some galaxies still fall below the minimum IRX$-\beta$ relation derived with standard dust cloud models.

claims.hypothesis: High-z galaxies have warmer IR SEDs than z<4 priors
claims.experiment: Correlate T with metallicity and sSFR in local samples and three analogs
claims.result: Low-metallicity, high-sSFR galaxies show higher T
claims.finding: Adopt T=60-90 K, raising L_FIR by ~0.6 dex

evidence.quote: This provides us with good evidence that the IR SEDs of high-redshift galaxies show a warm emission component

claims.hypothesis: Spatial offset of dust clouds from stars explains low IRX
claims.experiment: Modified Charlot & Fall model with cloud separation
claims.result: model reproduces low IRX and wide beta range

evidence.quote: Our model can quantitatively explain the low IRX values of the $z\sim5.5$ galaxies

limitations_admitted.value: Warm SED evidence is indirect, from local correlations and three analogs

evidence.quote: the evidence of a warmer IR SED in high-redshift galaxies is indirectly derived from correlations in local galaxies and three exemplary analogs

referee_caveats_inferred: Three analogs, one poorly constrained, support the temperature prior
ALMA data on analogs are only upper limits and play a minor role

missing_for_reproduction: tabulated Herschel photometry for local samples

reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA is minor; SED recipe given but fitting details missing.
